title: Sign the Function
goal: Complete the signature and body so greeting works for any name.
hints: Parameters always need a type in Rust.
Quotes around a name make it a literal, not a variable.
explanation: A bare `name` parameter is a syntax error: Rust has no inference at function boundaries, so every parameter is `name: Type`. Text arrives as `&str`. In the body, `name` interpolates the parameter; `"name"` would compile but print the word name for every caller, which the tests catch at runtime.
